Highly resolved, representative load profiles and projections by data center type • Clear need for higher-resolution load data for different data center types1 to evaluate demand flexibility and study bulk system cost projection scenarios • Ongoing national lab efforts to produce hourly industrial load profiles at the county level • Different estimation approaches with pros/cons for each • Example input data: ◦ Consumption: Aggregate consumption, hourly or sub-hourly power usage effectiveness (PUE), sub-process load factors ◦ Data center types and characteristics: Standard facility characteristics, equipment and IT stacks, IT nameplate power capacity ratings, rack counts, servers by class, etc. ◦ Point locations and footprints: Geospatial point locations from Baxtel, facility footprints where available ◦ Region and/or climate zone: Ambient weather for modeling of cooling processes—for example, from National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) or National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB) datasets ◦ Rates and tariff structure: To allow for possibility of price- or behavior-based demand 1For example, EPRI has stated that “there is limited empirical data for the temporal pattern of actual power use for different DC configurations…Different types of data centers exhibit a variety of load patterns based on component configurations and system specifications.” “Powering Data Centers.” 2024.
